subject: Data deletion evidence — backup & cross-region scope (SOC 2 / ISO)
messages:
From: Jake Miller <jake.miller@finsecure.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-04T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Data deletion evidence request — backups & cross-region replicas

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. For our SOC 2 / ISO assessment we need evidence that deletions and retention policies cover the following:
- Primary datastore TTLs and enforcement (per-customer mapping)
- Backup retention and automated purging (including cross-region snapshots and offsite replicas)
- Proof that deleted customer data has been removed from all restore points (or an auditable exception)
- KMS / key rotation and whether that can be used as part of cryptographic erasure proof

Can you share the exports/logs and any runbook or playbook that shows how a customer deletion request flows to backups/replicas? Prefer CSV/flat exports and runbook links.

I've attached our questionnaire for fields we typically need.

Thanks,
Jake
FinSecure Audit Team
Attachment: auditor_questionnaire.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jake Miller <jake.miller@finsecure.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion evidence request — backups & cross-region replicas

Hi Jake — thanks for the checklist, forwarding to the right owners and including a preliminary bundle below. Please confirm whether a combined audit-log + manifest per deletion event will meet your evidence requirements, or if you need exported snapshots of object stores as well.

What I'm attaching now:
- redwood_audit_log_export_20250802.csv (tokenized event-level deletes: event_id, resource_type, resource_id_hashed, initiator, timestamp, final_state)
- s3_lifecycle_policies.txt (human-readable export of lifecycle rules by bucket class)
- backup_retention_matrix.xlsx (matrix: snapshot_class -> retention_days -> replica_regions)
- drive link to runbook (see related_links)

High-level mapping:
- Customer object storage: TTL set at application layer; objects are lifecycle-tagged for S3 lifecycle rules (30/90/365 days depending on class).
- Backups: incremental snapshots stored in region primary; cross-region replicas retained per retention matrix. Snapshots older than retention are pruned by retention job; deletion job emits audit-events and a manifest entry.
- Replicas/offsite: replica deletion is driven by the same manifest, but some legacy replica flows have a 24–72 hour reconciliation delay; we flag those for auditors.
- KMS: rotation is monthly; we can provide rotation report and CMK metadata but note cryptographic erasure is not used as primary deletion proof today.

Open items (we'll add these artifacts in follow-up):
- KMS rotation proof (we can provide logs)
- Replica deletion manifests and a sample deletion-run output

If that scope looks right, I'll attach the KMS rotation report and a deletion-run log in my follow-up.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security Ops — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
Attachment: redwood_audit_log_export_20250802.csv; s3_lifecycle_policies.txt; backup_retention_matrix.xlsx

Irene — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups:
1) For KMS: can you provide a timestamped rotation audit (who/when/key-id) and whether any keys have been retired such that old ciphertext cannot be decrypted?
2) For replicas: we need an example manifest that shows the replica resource IDs and a post-deletion reconciliation result (i.e., replica not found / tombstone).
3) Runbook: do you have a runbook that SRE can execute to force-delete a customer in a test environment (so we can validate the end-to-end removal)?

If you can provide those three items, we should be able to close the loop. Reference: JIRA-FINSEC-447.

Thanks,
Jake

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jake Miller <jake.miller@finsecure.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-06T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion evidence request — backups & cross-region replicas

Jake — pushing the artifacts you requested. Summary of what's attached and how to interpret each item follows the attachments.

Attachments in this message (zipped originally; listed individually here):
- kms_rotation_report.pdf — rotation history for CMKs used in storage encryption (columns: rotation_date, key_id, operator, status). Note: we rotate monthly and retire keys after 18 months per policy.
- replica_deletion_manifest_stub.txt — sample manifest entries emitted by the replica deletion service (resource_hashed_id, region, snapshot_id, deletion_timestamp, deletion_event_id).
- deletion_run_results_20250805.log — output from a test deletion run in a sandbox customer (includes reconciliation steps and reconciliation_id).
- runbook_deletion_workflow.md — SRE runbook for manual forced deletion in test and guidance for production (includes safety checks and approvals).

How to read the artifacts:
- The audit_log CSV ties deletion API calls to the manifest entries and to storage-layer events. Each deletion has an event_id that appears in the manifest and the deletion_run_results log.
- Backups and snapshots: snapshot_class determines retention (see backup_retention_matrix.xlsx). For example, "standard" snapshots are retained 90 days; long-term exports 365 days. When TTL triggers, the retention job issues a delete that generates a manifest entry; the replica deletion job reconciles and reports missing replicas as tombstones.
- Timing and edge cases: legacy replicas may show a 24–72 hour reconciliation lag; we include a reconciliation window column in the matrix and a reconciliation SLA in the runbook.
- KMS: rotation report shows active/retired keys. Retired keys are flagged; ciphertext produced with retired keys requires key recovery workflows (rare) — we do not rely solely on crypto-erasure for compliance evidence.

Next steps I recommend for your evidence pack:
1) Use redwood_audit_log_export_20250802.csv + replica_deletion_manifest_stub.txt + deletion_run_results_20250805.log as the primary linkage proof for 3 sample deletion events.
2) We can generate a filtered export showing the three sample event_ids and include object hashes if you'd like.
3) If FinSecure requires cryptographic erasure evidence, we can discuss a scope to map CMK material lifecycle to data lifecycle; otherwise the manifest+log approach is our standard SOC/ISO evidence.

Happy to set up a quick walkthrough with Neha (engineering lead for backups) and Laura (compliance) if you want to review artifacts.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachment: kms_rotation_report.pdf; replica_deletion_manifest_stub.txt; deletion_run_results_20250805.log; runbook_deletion_workflow.md
